answer:
Let the initial capacitor be  
\[
C_0=6\,\mu{\rm F},\qquad V_0=12\,{\rm V}
\]
so
\[
Q_0=C_0V_0=72\,\mu{\rm C},
\qquad
U_0=\frac12C_0V_0^2=432\,\mu{\rm J}.
\]
After inserting the dielectric, the capacitance doubles:
\[
C'=2C_0=12\,\mu{\rm F}.
\]

### 1. Battery disconnected
Charge is constant:
\[
Q'=Q_0=72\,\mu{\rm C}.
\]
Then
\[
V'=\frac{Q'}{C'}=6\,{\rm V},
\]
and
\[
U'=\frac{Q'^2}{2C'}
=\frac{(72\,\mu{\rm C})^2}{2(12\,\mu{\rm F})}
=216\,\mu{\rm J}.
\]
Thus
\[
\Delta U=U'-U_0=216-432=-216\,\mu{\rm J}.
\]
The stored energy decreases by \(216\,\mu{\rm J}\). This energy appears as mechanical work done by the electric field pulling the dielectric into the capacitor.

### 2. Battery connected
Voltage remains \(12\,{\rm V}\). Thus
\[
Q'=C'V'= (12\,\mu{\rm F})(12\,{\rm V})=144\,\mu{\rm C},
\]
and
\[
U'=\frac12C'V^2
=\frac12(12\,\mu{\rm F})(12\,{\rm V})^2
=864\,\mu{\rm J}.
\]
So
\[
\Delta U=864-432=+432\,\mu{\rm J}.
\]
The extra charge supplied by the battery is
\[
\Delta Q=Q'-Q_0=144-72=72\,\mu{\rm C}.
\]
Therefore the work done by the battery is
\[
W_{\rm battery}=V\Delta Q
=(12\,{\rm V})(72\,\mu{\rm C})
=864\,\mu{\rm J}.
\]

The energy balance is
\[
W_{\rm battery}=\Delta U+W_{\rm mech}.
\]
Hence
\[
W_{\rm mech}=864-432=432\,\mu{\rm J}.
\]
So half of the battery’s work increases the stored field energy, and the other half is mechanical work done by the field pulling the dielectric into the capacitor.

### Summary
\[
\boxed{\begin{aligned}
&\text{Battery disconnected: } \Delta U=-216\,\mu{\rm J},\\
&\text{Battery connected: } \Delta U=+432\,\mu{\rm J},\\
&W_{\text{battery, supplied}}=864\,\mu{\rm J}.
\end{aligned}}
\]
In the connected case, \(432\,\mu{\rm J}\) is stored and \(432\,\mu{\rm J}\) is released as mechanical work on the dielectric. In the disconnected case, the field energy drops by \(216\,\mu{\rm J}\), which is also mechanical work done on the dielectric. If the insertion is quasistatic, an external agent must absorb these amounts; otherwise they may appear as kinetic energy and eventually heat.
